If you’re building a new cordless tool set, or updating your battery system, getting a cordless tool set can save you some money because these combos usually include batteries and a charger, which can be the most expensive part of your tool set. Here are a few of the best early Black Friday deals on cordless tool sets.

The Ryobi 6-tool 18-volt combo set is on sale for $199, 33% off its regular price at Home Depot. The Ryobi 18-volt drill and driver set is on sale for $99, 34% off its usual price at Home Depot. The set comes with a drill, an impact driver, two 1.5-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a great starter set because it has the first two tools you need for a cordless kit and it comes with batteries so you can expand your set for cheaper as you develop your skills.

The Ryobi 4-tool, 4-volt project set is on sale for $99, 61% off its typical price at Home Depot. This set comes with a rotary tool, a project light, a glue pen, a mini drill, two rechargeable batteries, a charging cable, a set of starter rotary bits, and three glue sticks. This set is handy for DIY projects that require fine detail, like wood carving, craft projects, or framing pictures.

The DeWalt drill and driver combo set is on sale for $149, 38% off its regular price on Amazon. This set includes a drill, an impact driver, 2 1.5-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a good deal on a trusted brand for drills and drivers, and a good start for a cordless DIY tool set.

If you have a cordless tool set already and you want to expand your kit, or if you have a DIYer in your life who already has a particular brand of battery and you want to get them something they can use, a single tool deal can be just the thing.

The DeWalt 20-volt compact drill/driver is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 45% off its usual price. This tool comes with a 20-volt, 2-amp-hour battery and a charger, so it’s ready to use out of the box. It’s a good first tool for a set.

The Milwaukee 18-volt impact wrench is on sale at Home Depot for $199, 68% off its typical price. This tool comes with two 5-amp-hour batteries and a charger, so it’s ready to use out of the box. This is a good tool for driving bolts through tough materials and for automotive projects.

This is an excellent addition to your emergency roadside tool set because you can use it to inflate a car tire with the charged 18-volt batteries.

The Makita 18-volt cordless electric 2-inch brad nailer is on sale on Amazon for $324, 38% off its regular price. This is a tool-only deal, so you’ll need a Makita 18-volt battery and charger to use it. This is a good tool for attaching trim or paneling.

#3455. 10 Best Richie Rich Visual Gags Of All Time

Richie Rich is one of the most enduringly popular icons to come out of the old Harvey Comics universe, beyond mainly Casper the Friendly Ghost. His affable personality basically projects the average middle-class kid's temperament in the mid-20th century onto the heir to a vast, cartoonish family fortune. He's the inversion of the ultra-privileged scion image people might imagine when thinking of an only child with virtually unlimited resources and the answer to all of life's problems being money. And in the particular era beyond his Little Dot debut, the Richie Rich comic book covers of the original eponymous series from 1960-1991 conveyed these through fun visual gag illustrations.

These covers often told a story within themselves of how Richie would deploy wealth-based solutions to life's troubles with a cheerful smile all along the way. Other covers would feature him enjoying childhood like any other kid, but with vast resources at his disposal to heavily stylize them or just for a comedic display of ostentatious wealth.

The Far Side loves to throw absurd filters over everyday life, and one thing that everyone deals with is money. Here are the 10 funniest about money!

Extreme cases, though, can show how silly, impractical, or simply impossible it is to theme everything around money, particularly when it comes to his flair for odd, cash-themed personal vehicles.But Warren Kremer in particular did a wonderful job in rendering a Jetsons-like aspirational image, not of futurism, but of an optimistic, empathetic young boy with an incredible fortune and friends to share it with.

Part of Richie Rich's charm is in just how he'll try to integrate into regular society while putting his huge cash reserves to use at any turn. In this case, it's turning wads of cash into impromptu padding, even though it'd make far more sense for conventional shoulder pads, let alone just being safer. It's certainly an unusual way to bulk up his shoulders, especially with pads visibly discarded to the right. But how else can Richie's fortune be put to use in an otherwise fair game of football?

There's something so charming about how Richie, with all the money in the world, is still very much a kid content to play with toys. But in classic Richie Rich fashion, this particular display of wealth is one of the most obnoxious and silly ones ever drawn. Tethered to his massive super yacht in the distance, Richie rides his tiny gilded dinghy so he can then string his tiny toy sailboat along. After all, kids like Richie get bored of staying in any place long enough, even if it's a comically massive boat that'd make Jeff Bezos jealous.

This particular visual gag is the type that starts simply by showing the unnecessary added features of Richie's surfboard, down to a rear view mirror, and gets more absurd the more one thinks about it. With a steering wheel, a motor, and presumably a rudder, this surfboard suddenly becomes more of a boat with absolutely no guardrails, safety being sacrificed on the altar of status. But it's okay, he's got his golden luxury features, and even a bench seat for if he wants to relax while catching the next big wave.

There's something to be said about just how many hobbies Richie Rich picks up, but there's another matter entirely for the ability to create entirely new sound. With a dollar sign joining otherwise typical notes on a musical staff, Richie appears to have found a new key only he can play in. But a golden violin also presents other hilarious problems: Richie would hardly settle for gold-plated half measures, so it'd be much heavier, and acoustically terrible. But if one were to safely gamble on what that mysterious note would sound like, it'd likely be "cha-ching!"

One of the most adorable early Richie Rich visual gags, this renders the classic idiom about the goose that lays the golden egg present in all sorts of pop culture media. The gag turns even that goose into a plurality, laying countless eggs to create a sort of one-percenter easter egg hunt. The gag is perfectly simple while having fun with Richie Rich's particular quirk, without resorting to elaborate gadgets or even a kid's projected image of wealth. It's just a kid frolicking and having fun, at no added expense and farming immense profit.

Much like gathering eggs or playing with toy boats, Richie Rich as a comic always adds a twist to how its star addresses completely mundane situations. This cover's not even the first one rendering a camp or even a campfire scene, but it's also a far humbler scene, until readers quickly zero in on the fact that Richie is using a precious gem ring the size of a jawbreaker as a magnifying glass to light his fire. It's perfectly silly, but also far from the most over-the-top solution he could deploy in such a situation, and frankly not bad problem-solving, provided the ruby boulder on his hand functions enough like a lens to make it possible.

Money is said not to be the solution to all of life's problems, but to Richie Rich, it comes awfully close, especially if one has enough of it on hand. In the case of a badly damaged landing gear wheel of his private jet, Richie patches the gaping gash with haphazardly-placed dollar bills, functioning both as a tire plug and apparently as a chock.

The pilot seems to trust this plug will hold, but the repair truck better be the one to reap the cash reward for a job well done in the end. Richie's a good kid for pitching in, though, both by paying upfront and helping with the labor. It's a solid example of his "Noblesse Oblige" traits, or tendencies to dutifully use his resources to help those around him, even if it hardly seems like a solution that'd ever truly work.

With the Rich family, their vast wealth means even simple Christmas celebrations involve massive displays of wealth, in this case being a towering behemoth of a Christmas tree. In fact, it's so tall that Richie Rich himself flies his gilded personal helicopter so he can carefully hang ornaments around its highest points. One has to wonder what is more of a pain, dressing the tree, or tearing it all down once the holidays are over.

There's nothing inherently wrong with Richie Rich keeping a consistent style in mind, but this visual gag is particularly funny for anybody who's ever participated in the wood car racing hobby, and wanted to carve an elaborate design. Beyond the question of how good the steering would be (and Richie's lack of a helmet, which is aside the point) it's just funny seeing the absolute aerodynamic nightmare that is this dollar sign design, and how he'd likely be trailing far behind the other racers in any other case.

But with Richie Rich comics, a healthy suspension of disbelief and a sense of humor can go a long way, even if this car doesn't seem to have a suspension, and really can't go a long way.

One of the most innocent examples of Richie Rich just being an ordinary, this image of him playing cowboy still shows he can't help but show how much he's all about the money. The dollar sign he manages to form while twirling the rope in the air is impressive, but whether the illustration was faulty or, hopefully intentional, it looks more like it's an absolutely lousy lasso. In fact, it looks just like no loop was formed at all, but with a knot in the middle, meaning Richie Rich looks less like a cowboy and more like a juvenile Le Chiffre hitting the dude ranch.

#3454. Gerard Butler’s Action Streaming Hit Is Officially Being Removed From Netflix

The action thriller genre is full of heroes who put their lives at risk for the greater good or personal vengeance. Recently, Keanu Reeves’ John Wick franchise does it best, as our favorite ex-assassin goes on a rampage after his dog is killed. Features like Jason Statham’s The Beekeeper and A Working Man woo audiences with the trope and keep them in their seats with slick action.

Among such entertaining features is Gerard Butler’s Law Abiding Citizen. Directed by F. Gary Gray, whose works include The Fate of the Furious and The Italian Job, and written by Kurt Wimmer, scribe for action films like The Beekeeper, Point Break, and Salt. The movie follows an honorable family man, Clyde Shelton (Butler), whose wife and daughter are murdered in a home invasion. He hopes for justice, but a rising prosecutor named Nick Rice (Jamie Foxx) cuts a deal with one of the killers in exchange for testimony.

The feature highlights the themes of friction between moral justice and legal procedure. It also cautions against the corrupting nature of vengeance as we see Butler’s character starting with sympathy but going on a full rampage and killing innocent people, which makes this movie extremely dark when compared to other entries in the genre. It was a modest success, earning $127.9 million at the box office against a budget of $53 million, although it got mixed reviews. It can be seen in the movie's Rotten Tomatoes score wherein critics awarded it 26% while the audience gave it a much higher score of 75%. No doubt the movie is proving a compelling rewatch on streaming as it keeps popping up on various streaming charts.

For fans who’d love to revisit the film, time is running out as Netflix is scrubbing Law Abiding Citizen from its digital streaming library at the end of the month. Butler seamlessly transforms from a man filled with grief to one who’s consumed with vengeance. Foxx effectively portrays a man slowly realizing his own complicity in a broken system. His smug confidence in the opening act transforms into genuine desperation and guilt as Clyde dismantles his life.

Check out Law Abiding Citizen on Netflix before it leaves the platform on November 30. Stay tuned to Collider for more such updates.

#3449. MagSafe Monday: Pelican’s MagSafe wallet is built for the people who still carry cash

I’ve been on a Pelican kick this fall. It started with the Pelican MagSafe Wallet, then the Pelican MagSafe Battery Pack, and the reason is pretty simple: once the weather turns cool, I want iPhone accessories built for the outdoors because I am outside more. The Pelican Protector Magnetic Money Clip Wallet is really helpful is you want something rugged, but also supports holding cash.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Most magnetic wallets are a simple card sleeve and nothing else. If you carry a few $5 bills for tips, cash-only places, etc., you end up folding them around a card and hoping they don’t slip out. The Pelican Protector Magnetic Money Clip Wallet has a stainless steel money clip on the outside of the wallet, so the cash rides on the back, where you can access it without pulling your credit cards out. It’s the same hard-shell construction as the rest of Pelican’s lineup, with the same MagSafe magnets.

The wallet holds up to five cards, which is just about perfect for my use cases. That covers my Driver’s license, debit card, and a few credit cards. There are ridges inside that push the cards up when you squeeze, so you’re not digging with your nails. A steel plate blocks RFID scanning, and the shell is rated IPX4 for water, which covers rain, etc.

Pelican calls its drop protection military-grade, which is what every accessory company says. A more useful way to think about it is that it’s a hard-shell wallet rather than a leather or silicone one.

Two things to know going in with this wallet. Five cards plus a clip of cash makes for a thick back on your phone, so this isn’t a very slim wallet. If you’re replacing a money clip, you are basically combining the two into one.

If you never carry much cash, the original Pelican wallet is the better pick. If you do want to carry a bunch of cash, the Pelican Protector Magnetic Money Clip Wallet is an awesome pickup.

The Pelican Protector Magnetic Money Clip Wallet is available on Amazon and directly from Pelican.

#3448. Dungeon Crawler Carl Officially Replaces Carl Ahead Of Book 9

If you're all caught up on Dungeon Crawler Carl and can't wait for Book 9, you're definitely not alone. The series has exploded in popularity in recent months and anticipation for the final two-volume conclusion is through the roof. Author Matt Dinniman has recently released a few teaser chapters on his Patreon page, which is well worth supporting whether you're new to the series or have been around since the beginning.

Aside from the Patreon teasers, there's plenty to keep fans busy ahead of Book 9's release, which is going by the working title The Beautiful Place. Dungeon Crawler Carl Book 1 is actually getting a fancy new Deluxe Edition next week, which includes an "interview" of Matt Dinniman conducted by Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk herself. Further, the RPG and Unstoppable deck-building game are slated to hit retail later this month.

However, you may have missed one new Dungeon Crawler Carl release that's well worth checking out, and it's one that "replaces" Carl as the main character and puts Donut in the spotlight for a hilarious and quirky new experience called Mama's Night Off.

With Dungeon Crawler Carl continuing to expand into new territory, it was probably only a matter of time before Princess Donut got her own video game. Mama's Night Off is a free, browser-based arcade game released in July 2026 by Maeve Chocolate, a Seattle-based chocolate company formerly known as Seattle Chocolate. It's a hilarious little experience that puts Donut front and center, and it's surprisingly addictive.

It's a very simple game, but well worth a look, as players must use Princess Donut's laser eyes to blast falling cherries, earning as many points as possible before the 30-second timer expires. There's no complicated tutorial or elaborate RPG progression, just a frantic challenge that encourages repeat attempts to beat your high score. The game even features a cheeky "New Achievement!" message and lets players challenge their friends.

The game was actually created to celebrate Maeve's official Dungeon Crawler Carl chocolate collaboration, specifically the Virgin Dirty Shirley truffle bar inspired by Donut's favorite drink. (Yes, we know a Virgin Dirty Shirley is just a Shirley Temple, that's the joke.) The bar combines dark chocolate, cherries, white chocolate, and popping candy for a fizzy twist. The partnership has since expanded to include Carl's Sweet Pota-toe Chips, a milk chocolate bar with crunchy sweet potato chips, alongside a Benefactor Bonbon Box and Station Mimic Gift Set.

You can play Mama's Night Off at Maeve's website here.

However, one of the best things about Mama's Night Off is that it features entirely new voice recordings from Jeff Hays, the beloved narrator behind the Dungeon Crawler Carl audiobooks and future voice of the live-action Donut in the upcoming television adaptation. Hays recorded fresh dialogue for both Donut and the Dungeon AI, including some hilarious "pew" sound effects accompanying Donut's attacks. The additional audio gives the otherwise simple game some of the personality that makes the audiobooks so amazing.

Granted, Mama's Night Off isn't the full-fledged Dungeon Crawler Carl video game fans might be dreaming of, but it's a wonderfully silly distraction while waiting for The Beautiful Place. With Book 9 still on the horizon and plenty of other exciting projects in development, it's a great reminder that Carl might be the franchise's namesake, but Princess Donut has always known she's the real star.

#3447. Chris Pratt Officially Addresses Star-Lord Return Amid James Gunn's DC Departure

Chris Pratt has been busy as ever in 2026 despite being years removed from his big-budget franchise roles, but that hasn’t stopped him from finding success at the box office. Pratt stumbled with the release of Mercy (co-starring Rebecca Ferguson) earlier this year, but despite an underwhelming performance in theaters, the movie went on to find success on Prime Video. Pratt swiftly returned to box office greatness thanks to his titular role in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, the sequel that grossed over $1 billion at the global box office. In the latter half of the year, Pratt has focused more on streaming projects like the second season of The Terminal List, which is now streaming on Prime Video. He’s soon to debut a new movie on Apple TV with Way of the Warrior Kid, which co-stars Linda Cardellini.

Most fans would agree that, despite all the new roles he’s taken on in the last few years, Pratt is still best known for his role as Star-Lord in the Guardians of the Galaxy movies. All three films were written and directed by James Gunn, who was the co-head of DC Studios along with Peter Safran for several years before stepping down from his duties earlier in the week. Fans around the world are already asking about what James Gunn is going to do next, with some speculating that he could return to Marvel for another Guardians movie. During a recent interview to promote the second season of The Terminal List, Pratt was asked about potentially returning to the Marvel universe for a new Star-Lord project, possibly one even under James Gunn. His answer might shock you:

“That would be awesome. I love working with James [Gunn]. He’s the man. I haven’t had the chance to speak with him since that news came out… it's always tough because anytime something like this comes up it could always become a headline. All I’ll say is I love James. He directed all three [Guardians of the Galaxy movies], and that’s pretty rare… so if he wanted to come back and bring it back, I would love that.”

At the end of Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, the card that played across the screen promised fans that “the legendary Star-Lord will return.” There’s been no official confirmation yet on which project will deliver on this promise, but most fans assume that Pratt will reprise the role in Avengers: Doomsday later this year. Still, Pratt told Collider last year that Marvel would follow through on the promise, so he certainly knows something that we don’t.

Stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of Chris Pratt’s future projects and check out the second season of The Terminal List on Prime Video.

#3446. Update Your iPhone to Prevent People From Seeing iMessages They Shouldn't

Has this ever happened to you? You add someone new to an iMessage group chat, and wonder, "Huh, can they see any of the messages from before they were added?" The answer to that question is supposed to be "no." By design, new iMessage group chat members are only privy to texts that arrive after they were added. When they join, it's essentially a blank slate, as if you just created the group for the first time. At least, that's how it's intended to work.

As it turns out, there's a bug with iMessage that may allow new group chat members to see texts from before they were added to the chat. That's a problem, and not just for the iPhone users out there talking smack about people before inviting them to join the group chat. It means iMessage, and Apple's platforms in general, aren't working like they're supposed to be. You don't have to be talking behind people's backs to not want new members seeing existing chats. Maybe you're planning a surprise party for someone, and add them to the group once everyone's in on the plan; maybe the texts in the chat aren't relevant to the current group, and the person joining simply does not need to access them.

That's not all: There exists another security flaw that could allow remote hackers to join an iMessage group and receive new messages. You might add a new user to a group chat and inadvertently invite them to read all existing messages, while at the same time being attacked by a bad actor who can then intercept all future messages. Not good.

Luckily, there's currently a fix for these problems. Apple patched (and revealed) the bugs, along with seven other security flaws, with a series of software updates on Monday for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro. Not all of the updates include patches for these two iMessage flaws—specifically, some of the updates for older Apple devices. But the rest, including iOS 27.2.1, macOS 27.2.1, macOS 26.7.3, macOS 15.8.3, watchOS 27.2.1, and visionOS 27.2.1, include the iMessage patches.

Each update includes its own list of patches, but, for this article, I'll take a look at the nine patches in iOS 27.2.1. You'll find the two iMessage bugs, plus seven other patches, in the list below:

AirPlay: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113968: Apple

App Intents: Impact: An app may be able to access sensitive user data. Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113963: László Várady

Bluetooth: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to corrupt process memory. Description: A use-after-free issue was addressed with improved memory management. CVE-2026-113970: Apple

brotli: Impact: Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption. Description: An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved input validation. CVE-2026-111497

CoreUtils: Impact: A malicious Bluetooth device may be able to establish a pairing without user interaction. Description: This issue was addressed with improved checks. CVE-2026-113965: Apple

CoreUtils: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts and pair with a device without user interaction. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113964: an anonymous researcher

Messages: Impact: A remote attacker may be able to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages. Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved validation. CVE-2026-113961: an anonymous researcher

Messages: Impact: A user added to an iMessage group may be able to access messages sent before they joined. Description: This issue was addressed by removing the vulnerable code. CVE-2026-113960: an anonymous researcher

Rapportd: Impact: An attacker on the same network may be able to bypass the rate limit on AirPlay pairing code attempts. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113969: Apple

For a full accounting of the patches included in the other security updates, check out Apple's official security releases site.

To install Apple's latest security updates, you'll simply need to update your device as you usually do. On iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro, head to Settings > General > Software Update; on Mac, go to System Settings > General > Software Update. Here, follow the on-screen instructions to download and install the latest version of your device's software.

Apple originally tested the new Health app in the iOS 27.2 beta, but it was removed before the public launch. The company said from the start, though, that the app would return and ship later this year, now confirmed with iOS 27.3.

Selfie Sing lets you create karaoke videos of yourself using the iPhone’s camera and Apple Music’s built-in lyrics feature. As seen above, the feature puts lyrics onscreen below your camera feed so you can sing along to your favorite songs then share your video on social.

It won’t be for everyone, but Selfie Sing is a fun addition that represents one of Apple’s few attempts at a social-centric offering.

When iPhone Duo launched, it included a variety of exclusive features related to StandBy mode. But with iOS 27.3, Apple is bringing these StandBy improvements to all iPhones.

Additionally, iOS 27.3 lets you create multiple versions of each face for easily swiping between them. These features won’t be new for iPhone Duo users, but it’s great to see Apple bring them to more iPhone models.

Which iOS 27.3 features are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments.

Karin Slaughter adapts her own novel in this six-episode Peacock series

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Although she has a long way to go before reaching Harlan Coben status, novelist Karin Slaughter creates similarly addictive yet disposable crime thrillers, full of sudden twists and complicated backstory.

I get a similar feeling from watching TV adaptations of both authors’ books, eager to tune in for the next episode but a bit let down when all of the secrets are revealed. That was my response to the first TV series based on a Slaughter novel, the 2022 Netflix hit “Pieces of Her,” and it’s the same for the new Slaughter series, "The Good Daughter."

There’s more emotional depth to Slaughter’s stories than Coben’s, and “The Good Daughter” is anchored by two strong performances from Meghann Fahy and Rose Byrne as estranged sisters Charlie and Sam Quinn. The six-episode Peacock original series, adapted by Slaughter herself from her 2017 novel, is more briskly paced than “Pieces of Her,” although it still gets bogged down in lengthy stretches of exposition.

It deals with some heavy themes, but always in a pulpy, airport-novel kind of way, making it an easy binge despite the dark subject matter.

Set in the fictional Georgia town of Pikeville, “The Good Daughter” shifts between past and present as it tells the connected stories of two terrible incidents involving Charlie and Sam (played as children by Drew Cheek and Audrey Grace Marshall). Their father Rusty (Brendan Gleeson) is a steadfast local defense attorney who frequently incurs the wrath of the corrupt legal system run by the powerful Coin family.

When he angers the wrong people, the Quinns’ house gets burned down, and then they’re attacked by two gunmen in their new home while Rusty is out. The assailants kill Charlie and Sam’s mother, Gamma (Olivia Williams), and the two young girls barely get away.

Decades later, Charlie still lives in Pikeville, working as a defense lawyer alongside her father and separated from her husband Ben (Michael Dorman), an assistant district attorney. She finds herself in the wrong place at the wrong time when she witnesses the aftermath of a shooting at the local high school, and soon she’s deeply involved in defending the shooter, a scared and possibly mentally disabled young woman named Kelly Wilson (Shayna Benardo). After he’s incapacitated, Rusty calls in Sam for help, and she arrives from New York City, where she’s been working as a patent lawyer.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

That’s just some of the set-up for this overstuffed story, which can get a bit unwieldy as it moves back and forth across time periods and works out all of the intricate, overlapping relationships among the characters.

Of course, everyone in town is hiding something, and that includes the Quinns, who have to reveal their own long-buried secrets while searching for the truth about what actually happened at the high school, where the principal and one student were shot dead.

In the hands of lesser actors, “The Good Daughter” could have come across as low-rent exploitation, but Fahy and Byrne find the honesty and vulnerability in their characters, and the show succeeds as a story about sisters learning to trust and care for each other again.

As the present-day story begins, Charlie and Sam haven’t seen each other in 10 years, and Sam initially intends to spend only a day in town to help Rusty get back on his feet. But the more they’re together, the more they renew their connection, while also pushing each other’s buttons.

Fahy and Byrne have convincing sisterly chemistry, and it’s easy to believe that these people care deeply for one another and also carry deep resentment. The family dynamic is ultimately more engaging than the mystery of the school shooting, and the resolutions of the past and present storylines aren’t tied together as closely as might be expected.

Both Charlie and Sam are holding onto issues from the day their mother was murdered, and those revelations are cathartic, while the solution to the present-day mystery just feels like wrapping up loose ends.

Once the pieces start to fall into place, it’s not difficult to see where the story is going, and the final episode offers a string of long explanations that clear up every little question. Like the many Coben shows, “The Good Daughter” is both complicated and superficial, and it’s unlikely to linger in viewers’ minds for long.

That doesn’t mean it isn’t worth the time, though, especially for Coben fans or anyone who enjoyed seeing Fahy in fellow beach-read adaptations “The Perfect Couple” and “Sirens.” I was never hesitant to press play on the next episode, but I also found it easy to walk away at the end.

“The Good Daughter” premieres Nov. 12 on Peacock

#3443. Apple to open new Developer Center in Istanbul as part of broader Turkey investment

Apple today announced a long-term investment in Turkey, with seven new facilities focused on app development and manufacturing set to open in the country starting next year. Here are the details.

In a press release issued on its Turkish Newsroom (via MacRumors), Apple today announced a series of long-term investments in Turkey.

The announcement comes as former CEO and current executive chairman Tim Cook visits the country, as he’s been sharing on X.

Merhaba Istanbul! What a stunning view from the Grand Bazaar this morning alongside talented creator Cem Başak. Thrilled to visit this remarkable country! pic.twitter.com/c4daBBXe1l

The company’s investment in Turkey will be three-pronged, with the opening of five new Apple Developer Academies, one Apple Developer Center, and one Apple Manufacturing Academy.

Apple says it will open five new developer academies across Turkey over the next three years, with the first opening in Istanbul in 2027, alongside its new developer center. The Apple Manufacturing Academy, meanwhile, is set to open in Ankara in 2028.

Here’s Cook commenting on today’s announcement (translation ours):

“Apple has been serving our customers and communities in Turkey for 35 years. With this new commitment, we are proud to support the next generation of innovative entrepreneurs in the years ahead. […] Turkey’s developer community is developing apps used around the world. Meanwhile, small and medium-sized businesses stand out as organizations creating opportunities throughout the country. This investment provides developers and businesses with access to the training and resources they need to take their brightest ideas even further, as well as to Apple experts.”

Apple explained that its developer academies will offer “free, intensive nine-month programs focused on coding, design, marketing, project management, and artificial intelligence technologies,” while the developer center “will provide developers, entrepreneurs, and start-ups with a hands-on learning experience by providing access to the latest tools, technologies, and resources, as well as Apple experts and events.”

As for its manufacturing academy in Ankara, which will mark the company’s first Apple Manufacturing Academy outside the US, it will “provide free training and consultancy to small and medium-sized businesses, students and innovative entrepreneurs.”

Led by Apple experts, the curriculum will help participants adopt AI and intelligent manufacturing techniques through courses on machine learning technology, predictive maintenance, advanced automation, and robotics, as well as interactive workshops on lean operations and production efficiency.

#3442. This AirPods Feature Fixed My Biggest Problem With Listening to Podcasts to Fall Asleep

We're highlighting the small changes—from useful new gadgets, to fresh productivity techniques, to efficient hacks—that are improving our lives on a weekly basis.

There's lots to recommend about podcasts (and lots of podcasts to recommend), but one of their biggest benefits—for me, anyway—has little to do with what a particular show is about or even who hosts it: They're great for dissociating. I often have a podcast playing to distract my anxious brain from whatever I'm worried about (which, in 2026, is usually slightly less than everything).

Any time I don't want to be alone with my thoughts (say, when commuting or doing mindless chores), I can put on a podcast and be entertained by a couple of goobers talking about movies rather than spinning my wheels about my son's middle school applications. And there's no time I want to disassociate from reality more than bedtime.

For years I've used podcasts as a non-pharmaceutical sleep aid, and few things are more effective at helping me drop off quickly. Unfortunately, for years this also meant that once I fell asleep, the podcast kept playing. I have my podcast app set to delete episodes once finished, so if it was a show I cared about, I'd need to do a lot of redownloading and scrubbing through to find where I left off—that is, until I upgraded my earbuds to the AirPods Pro 3.

The AirPods Pro 3 launched alongside iOS 26 in the fall of 2025 with flashy features like vastly improved noise cancellation, Live Translation, Heart Rate Sensing, and hearing health settings, all of them quite welcome on a set of $250 premium earbuds. But the best new AirPods feature was one I didn't even know about when I decided to upgrade my four-year-old Beats Fit Pro.

In the AirPods settings (accessible via your iPhone's Settings app), if you tap Audio & Routing and scroll down, you'll see an option to turn on a setting called Pause Media When Falling Asleep. I don't think I need to tell you what this setting does. I can tell you that it works great.

According to Apple, the feature works by sensing when you're drifting off using the earbuds' built-in accelerometer to track your movement (or lack thereof). Once your earbuds have determined that you're falling asleep, they will pause your audio for you. And it isn't just the 2025 AirPods Pro 3 that support it—it also works on the second-generation AirPods Pro as well as the AirPods 4 and the AirPods 5.

I'll admit that I don't really understand how the AirPods Pro 3 can tell I'm falling asleep versus just lying very still, but I've never had them pause accidentally during active listening. Conversely, whenever I go back to the podcast I was listening to the night before, I'll find that the audio paused within a minute or two of the last part I remember hearing.

The AirPods Pro 3 aren't the only earbuds with a feature like this, but you'll most often only find it in dedicated "sleep earbuds" designed specifically for the purpose. While many of those offer extra health features like the ability to track your sleep cycles, I'm not really interested in that (my Apple Watch does most of it, and I don't look at that data anyway). Pausing my audio when I'm asleep is really all I need, and the AirPods Pro 3 do it well enough that I don't need to bother with a pair of dedicated bedtime buds.

High-end Garmin vs. flagship Apple Watch: Which will win?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I walked exactly 6,025 steps (manually counted) with the Apple Watch Series 12 on my left wrist and the Garmin Venu X1 on my right wrist to find out which is the more accurate fitness tracker.

I also logged my walk using the Strava app on my iPhone 16 Plus as a control for pace, distance, and climb. Read on to find out which of these two top-tier smartwatches came out on top, along with five takeaways from the workout data.

But first, how does the Apple Watch Series 12 stack up against the Garmin Venu X1 in terms of specs, features, and price? Apple's latest flagship starts at $399 for the small (42mm) non-cellular model.

The Garmin Venu X1 is a more premium device, with a starting price of $699, which technically makes it more of a direct competitor to the Apple Watch Ultra 4 than the Series 12.

Even so, both models sport bright, well-saturated displays, slim, sleek all-metal cases, and state-of-the-art heart rate trackers, multi-band GPS antennas, and barometric altimeters.

This is to say, when it comes to logging a basic walking workout, both the Apple Watch Series 12 and Garmin Venu X1 should be more than well-equipped to record my efforts with best-in-class precision. But is that actually the case? Check out the data for yourself below.

The Garmin Venu X1 packs nearly all of Garmin's best training features into a super-sleek all-metal case equipped with a stunning AMOLED touchscreen.

The Apple Watch Series 12 features the brand's latest heart rate sensor, support for lots of new holistic metrics and trend reports, a bright display, a comfortable case, and access to the world's largest smartwatch app store.

With step count being our primary grading metric, the Garmin Venu X1 decisively beats the Apple Watch Series 12. For any walk tests of this distance, I consider a step count tally within 100 steps of the actual count to be excellent and within a reasonable margin for error.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The Garmin Venu X1 meets the mark, overcounting by a forgivable 51 steps. The Apple Watch 12, on the other hand, overcounted by a much more notable 391 steps, a result that ultimately surprised me.

After all, in recent walk tests with the Apple Watch 12 vs. the Fitbit Edge and again vs. the Garmin Forerunner 170, the Series 12's step count total was pretty much right on the money.

For what it's worth, Strava's step count total of 6,032 was the closest of the bunch.

Apple and Garmin noted similar uphill effort, within five feet of each other, during my ~55-minute walk. However, these tallies appear to be somewhat inflated, assuming, of course, Strava's elevation data is correct, which seems likely, though not certain.

I say this because in past testing, the Garmin Venu X1 has proven time and again to be an incredibly reliable elevation tracker. The Apple Watch 12, on the flip side, does occasionally exaggerate uphill efforts.

Strava logged a little more distance than both the Apple Watch and Garmin — by about a tenth of a mile — and a quicker elapsed pace. And while Garmin's average elapsed pace is the slowest of the bunch, the Venu X1's moving pace metric is nearly identical to Strava's.

Garmin logged an average moving pace of 16 mins 18 secs per mile, not too far off from Strava's 16 mins 11 secs pace. Note: Apple doesn't log moving pace.

Despite some notable discrepancies in step count, climb, and pace, both the Apple Watch Series 12 and Garmin Venu X1 logged the exact same average and maximum heart rate for my walk.

I can't help but wonder if the outcome has anything to do with both watches being worn on stretchy, nylon straps secured with Velcro. I find this strap style fits more securely and comfortably than the dreadful silicone pin-and-buckle alternatives. Better fit = better heart rate data.

Finally, the Venu X1 used 1% more battery than the Series 12 to log my nearly one-hour walk. And even though Apple's climb and elapsed-pace metrics are a little closer to the control, the Garmin Venu X1 wins this head-to-head comparison with a closer total step count, distance, and moving-pace metrics.

Up next, I plan to test the Garmin Venu X1 against the Apple Watch Ultra 4 to see if it can pull off a repeat win. Until then, which smartwatches would you like me to test head-to-head next? And between the Garmin Venu X1 and Apple Watch 12, which do you prefer? Let me know below.

#3438. Before 'Reacher,' Alan Ritchson Starred in the Greatest Sci-Fi Franchise of All Time

Prime Video’s adaptation of Lee Child’s Reacher delighted and awed everyone as soon as Alan Ritchson was cast. Finally, there would be a book-accurate take on the drifting military man fighting on the side of good. Tom Cruise’s divisive interpretation of Jack Reacher was entertaining but far from what book fans had expected. Ritchson proved that he had the stature and the skills to pull off this beloved character. Hints about his rise to the top cropped up earlier in his career in one of the best sci-fi franchises of all time, The Hunger Games.

Ritchson was lethal in the second movie, Catching Fire, as a Victor from a Career district named Gloss. Due to the Quarter Quell that rocks all of Panem, he and his sister, Cashmere, are reaped from the existing pool of tributes, along with Katniss (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta (Josh Hutcherson). Though his dialogue is minimal, Ritchson commands the screen in his role as one of the many victims of The Hunger Games. Gloss and his sister are sent back to the Games even though they seemed to beat the system. They are admittedly among some of the tributes who volunteer, but it doesn’t make their stories any less tragic.

The Hunger Games has always been more than a YA romance with a love triangle. The franchise was unfairly lumped in with lesser dystopian series when it was the crowning jewel of the genre. Suzanne Collins’ work set itself apart in a story where the government uses children killing each other for entertainment. The message is even more subtle and harrowing when it comes to the Careers.

When Gloss is reaped, the Games lose all the luster for the Careers. In an interview with Caesar Flickerman (Stanley Tucci), he emphasizes that he isn’t going by choice. This is the sentiment shared by all the tributes, but in some ways, it is even more tragic when it comes to the Careers. These are tributes from only a couple of districts who buy into the Capitol’s propaganda. They train at special academies to enter the Games and volunteer to bring pride to their district.

The Hunger Games first touches on the tragedy of this setup with the sad death of Cato (Alexander Ludwig), who at the last moment understands that he is just another piece in President Snow’s (Donald Sutherland) games. The same can be said for Gloss and Cashmere, the brother-sister duo who won their games back-to-back. Just like the rest of the Victors, they oppose their treatment from the Capitol, which has made it painfully obvious that there are no winners in a fascist regime.

The Careers are used to create the illusion that there is nothing wrong with Panem. These are people who volunteer to enter a gallant pageant, which is a reminder of what the country has lost. Many of them are brainwashed to believe that it is their duty to conform to the standards of the Capitol. Other Districts like 12 don’t fall prey to these illusions because they live in such excruciating poverty. Even so, Careers are victims of the Capitol just like everyone who isn’t President Snow. The Hunger Games is a thoughtful franchise that keeps gaining traction because of how relevant it remains to this day.

#3436. Report: Apple saved over $5 billion in taxes through Singapore and Ireland in 2026

A new Financial Times report reveals how Apple saved billions in taxes in 2026 by shifting profits through Singapore and Ireland. Here are the details.

A few days ago, Apple published its annual Form 10-K, as required by the SEC, containing detailed information about its financial performance and operations for its 2026 fiscal year.

Included in the form, as the FT noted, is information regarding how Apple reduced its tax bill by billions of dollars through its operations in Singapore and Ireland.

For years, Apple’s tax arrangements in Ireland were the subject of scrutiny, culminating in a 2024 ruling by the EU’s top court that required the company to pay €13 billion in back taxes. Apple completed the payment in 2025.

That came a few years after Apple announced plans to bring most of its $252 billion in overseas cash back to the US, following tax reforms introduced during Donald Trump’s first administration.

Since then, to discourage companies from shifting profits to countries with lower tax rates, more than 130 countries have agreed to introduce a minimum corporate tax rate of 15% for large multinational companies, as part of a 2021 initiative coordinated by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

Under the agreement, companies that pay less than 15% in a particular country may face additional taxes to make up the difference. The new rules also resulted in an additional $2.5 billion in taxes for Apple in Singapore in 2026, according to the company’s SEC filing.

Ireland adopted the new rules in 2024, followed by Singapore in 2025.

Back to the FT’s report, it notes that new US accounting rules now require publicly traded companies to disclose when their taxes on overseas profits differ significantly from the 21% US federal corporate tax rate.

These new requirements revealed that Apple saved $2.7 billion in taxes through Singapore in 2026, surpassing the $2.6 billion it saved through Ireland.

If Apple had been taxed on all of its global profits in 2026 at the US federal rate, it would have incurred a total bill of $33bn — demonstrating the scale of the $5bn tax reduction it received from booking profits in Ireland and Singapore. The company incurred corporation taxes totalling $27bn this year.

The FT also noted that Apple’s effective tax rate in Singapore fluctuated around 10% between 2023 and 2025, but is expected to approach 15% under the new rules. Singapore’s standard corporate tax rate is 17%.

Don't forget to mouse-proof these forgotten areas in your home

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I can usually cope well with most common household pests (spiders are a breeze) — but I absolutely draw the line at mice or any other rodent. And since the colder weather marks the onset of 'peak rodent season', I've made a point of mouse-proofing my home and gathering all the essential supplies to keep mice away.

Not only are these rodents notoriously hard to get rid of, but they can cause severe damage to your building's structure and property.

Yet in my bid to remove the obvious things that attract rats and mice to your home, it turns out I had completely missed several unexpected entry points.

According to pest experts, these particular entry points frequently go unnoticed — so let my surprise serve as your lesson: here's what you need to look for.

While I typically focus my mouse-proofing efforts on inspecting baseboards and ground-level entryways, I don’t ever think to look up. However, the roof is one of the most overlooked and surprising access points where mice can enter your home.

“The roofline is probably the most underestimated entry point,” states Ed Dolshun, Vice President of Business Development and Technical Director at Catchmaster.

“Homeowners instinctively look at ground level, but mice climb — walls, utility wires, tree branches — and enter from above. Roof rats are commonly found along piping, fences, and shrubbery, working their way up rather than in from the ground”.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

To prevent rats from entering through your exterior walls or roof, you need to seal off gaps with steel mesh or hardware cloth combined with sealant to block any holes.

What’s more, to keep mice from scaling your walls, make climbing as difficult as possible by trimming back high shrubs, overgrown tree branches, and other nearby vegetation.

Another forgotten place we often overlook is the small gaps under garage doors and sheds. “A gap as small as a quarter inch along the bottom seal is enough for a mouse to squeeze through,” says Dolshun. “Most people assume their garage door closes tight, though many don't”.

So how small could the gap be for a mouse to sneak its way in? “This is the detail that tends to surprise people most: a mouse needs a gap roughly the size of a dime to get in, and a rat needs only a quarter-sized opening,” adds Dolshun.

A mouse needs a gap roughly the size of a dime to get in, and a rat needs only a quarter-sized opening.

“And critically, if a rodent can fit its head through an opening, it can work the rest of its body through. That should change how you think about inspecting your home because you're not looking for obvious holes, but rather anything that small.”

Similarly, seal gaps and cracks around doors and windows with caulk or mesh wool.

Also, ensure that leaf piles and plant debris are regularly raked clear from entryways. Allowing these to accumulate creates an inviting, warm shelter where rodents can easily hide and dwell during the colder months.

So if you want to make your home completely mouse-proof, don’t miss these common overlooked areas — or else you may have to call in the pest experts in the long run.

#3429. ‘Boston Blue’ Brings Back a ‘CSI’ Legend, but Its Biggest Problem Remains

Jeffrey is a freelance features writer at Collider. He is an MPA-accredited entertainment journalist and a Tomatometer-approved critic based in the LA area. He graduated from the University of Texas at Austin with a Bachelor of Science in Radio, TV, & Film and a Bachelor of Arts in Theater.

The hit CBS series Boston Blue just pulled off a huge coup in the casting department. Emmy Award-winning actress Marg Helgenberger, a television legend and veteran of shows like CSI, will return to the network in the hit Blue Bloods spin-off. Helgenberger will make her series debut in the upcoming Season 2 episode "Bloodlines" on November 13, portraying Gwen Silver, the estranged biological mother of main cast member Sarah Silver (Maggie Lawson). Helgenberger makes a great addition to the series and the overall Blue Bloods saga. However, despite the stupendous casting choice, the show's biggest problem still needs to be addressed.

Boston Blue serves as both a continuation and spin-off of its flagship series Blue Bloods. Much like its predecessor, it showcases a multi-generational family of law enforcers with the Silvers. The main connective tissue between the two shows is Blue Bloods veteran Danny Reagan (Donnie Wahlberg) and his son, Sean Reagan (Mika Amonsen, who took over the role from Andrew Terraciano for the new series). Danny uprooted his life to move to Boston to mentor Sean in his own career as a police officer, while Danny also receives a fresh start in a new city, seeking to climb the ladder in his career. Boston Blue struggles to find a balance between these two narratives.

A great detective is really just a personality with a method attached, which is why we keep remaking the same four of them. Here is yours, what it says about you, and the case for them being the best in the business.

You let people think you are not a threat and then you simply never go away. Columbo is the only major detective show that tells you who did it in the first ten minutes, because the pleasure was never the puzzle, it was watching a rich man slowly realise he is in trouble.

You are the most interesting person in the room and you know exactly how to use it. Rian Johnson built Blanc as a gentleman detective who is also an outsider everywhere he goes, which lets him be charming at people who would never otherwise talk to him.

Everybody tells you everything, and you have never once asked them to. Jessica Fletcher is a crime novelist from a small town in Maine who is so warm and so obviously trustworthy that suspects confess to her essentially as a social courtesy.

You expect to be lied to and you are almost never disappointed. Chandler wrote Marlowe as a man with a rigid private code in a city that has none, which is why he takes the case, solves it, gets nothing out of it and takes the next one.

As great as it is to see a multi-ethnic Jewish family celebrating Shabbat in a weekly broadcast television series, it's strange that the Reagans are constantly present for the dinners. The Reagans are Roman Catholics, and although they respect the Silvers' religious practices, they aren't Jewish themselves. In Blue Bloods, the Reagan family would occasionally invite guests to their Sunday dinners, but those were rare exceptions rather than the rule.

Danny and Sean appear to join the Silvers for Shabbat dinner on a weekly basis. It’s great that the Reagans and Silvers have a close friendship and bond, but they haven't known each other too long. Since they aren't related, it doesn’t make sense that they join the Silvers for Shabbat dinner all the time. Shouldn't the Reagans set up their own Sunday dinners instead? It comes across as if the writers are attempting to forcibly mimic the weekly family dinner dynamic from Blue Bloods in Boston Blue, where it makes less sense.

One area that Boston Blue appears to be working on in Season 2 is establishing the hierarchy of the BPD and City Hall, a narrative structure that the series has struggled with before. Thus far, the series has introduced the BPD's chief, Lanigan (Ron Lea), who has appeared sparingly, but the commissioner has yet to appear. Beginning with its first season, Blue Bloods did a much better job of demonstrating the hierarchy of everyone's roles in the NYPD, including Frank Reagan's (Tom Selleck) relationship with the mayor’s office, Erin working in the District Attorney's office, Danny operating as a detective, and Jamie Reagan (Will Estes) as a patrolman.

Across all these characters and subplots, the series presented a strong overview of the Reagans and their career dynamics; yet, in Boston Blue, it feels like we’re two seasons in and still playing catch-up. It derives from the series struggling as a continuation of Blue Bloods while trying to forge its own identity. Boston Blue shouldn't copy the weekly family dinners simply because the Blue Bloods made them famous. Although improvements have been made in Season 2, with storylines involving BPD’s superior officers, such as Chief Lanigan and Sean and Jonah's new sergeant, Betina Ryan (Sydney Ozerov-Meyer), it would improve the show to include additional storylines showcasing the command structure of the BPD, as well as Mae Silver's (Gloria Reuben) office and their relationship with Mayor Jim Shaw (Brian Goodman).

Boston Blue sometimes appears at odds with its format, trying to balance the traditions and characters of Blue Bloods to lure in longtime fans of the original series, while still maintaining strong narrative focus on its new characters and family. It's simply not necessary for the Silvers and Reagans to be joined at the hip every week. Separate dinners would work fine, and maybe Sean and Danny could have their own Sunday dinners with Sean's girlfriend, Penny (Xochitl Gomez), at some point? Also, why not bring Penny to New York City to introduce her to the Reagans, or have the entire family visit Boston to set up a Sunday dinner with Sean, Penny, and Danny?

Marg Helgenberger joining the show is a positive development because it helps flesh out Sarah Silver's character arc and her relationship with her mother, whom we've never seen before. As a multi-ethnic blended family, the Silver family presents a strong family dynamic that's unique to Blue Bloods, and the show should explore the family's distinctness more in future episodes. This will further reinforce Boston Blue's fresh new storylines, rather than trying to come across as Blue Bloods-lite or Blue Bloods: The Sequel.

#3428. 10 Hacks Every Waze User Should Know

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

Waze is a crowdsourced navigation app designed to help you get where you're going as quickly and with as much information about your route as possible. Where Google Maps and Apple Maps offer relatively straightforward directions, Waze tries to outsmart these alternatives by integrating real-time community feedback about hazards, speed traps, road closures, and more. If you are switching to Waze or using it alongside your other navigation tools, these are the hacks to help you maximize everything the app has to offer.

If you find yourself losing track of time or running late for events, Waze can notify you when it's time to leave—based on your current location and live traffic—so you arrive on schedule. You can set up "Time to leave" reminders in advance for individual planned drives, or you can sync your calendar to receive notifications for scheduled events. Calendar sync connects to your device's default calendar app, but you can change this to a third-party alternative if you prefer. Calendar events must include a navigable address to trigger reminders, and you must select Plan a drive in Waze for the event.

Waze has a feature called "child reminders," which are notifications to check for children before you get out of the car. This is clearly an incredibly important use case, but you can also use these alerts for custom messages, like "Don't forget the groceries!" In Waze, tap the menu button > Settings > Reminders > Child reminder and select Custom message.

Variable speed limits, especially on unfamiliar routes, can result in you speeding when you don't mean to. But Waze can alert you if you exceed a customized speed threshold so you aren't caught by surprise or at higher risk of being ticketed. From the menu, go to Settings > Speedometer and turn on Show speedometer. Tap Speeding threshold to select what limit you want to trigger alerts, and turn on Alert at threshold if you want Waze to play a sound.

Waze offers a wealth of information on routes to help drivers navigate obstacles and hazards, but this can clutter your map and distract you from the most critical information, especially in congested, high-traffic areas. Waze says it limits and prioritizes alerts automatically, but you can actually customize which alerts you see based on what's most important to you. From the menu, go to Settings > Alerts and reports > Reports and select the relevant alerts.

In the same Alerts and reports menu, you can enable Alert while driving, which will give you an audio warning and an onscreen pop-up about your selected hazards. This allows you to run navigation via a different map app (like Google Maps or Apple Maps) in the foreground while still getting Waze data in the background.

Waze integrates with toll road and HOV lane passes, so if you have an express or fast lane subscription, your route will optimize for it. If you don't, Waze can still account for HOV lane eligibility if you tell it how many passengers are in your car. From the menu, go to Settings > Toll and HOV passes and tap the plus icon to add your pass(es) from the list. If you need to add your passenger count instead, you can do so from View routes and enable the HOV option.

If you're driving through an unfamiliar, highly congested, or poorly designed area, you can ask Waze to help you avoid tricky maneuvers, such as crossing multiple lanes of traffic or turning left at intersections without lights. This prioritizes ease over speed using protected green arrows, roundabouts, and right turns. From the menu, go to Settings > Navigation, Avoid difficult intersections and select Always. You can also ask Waze to avoid toll roads, ferries, freeways, and unpaved roads.

Waze has a built-in audio player that syncs with your preferred listening platform—such as Spotify, YouTube Music, and Pandora—so you can control your music without having to navigate between apps. (As Waze is a Google product, Apple Music isn't included.) Simply tap the music icon on the map to select your audio player and hit Accept. If you don't see the icon, go to Settings > Audio player and turn on Show on the map.

If you want to make audio directions more interesting, you can select a celebrity or character voice to help you navigate. Recent appearances include Bill Hader's Cat in the Hat and Ziggy Marley. Tap the speaker icon > Current voice to search for the voice or language you want to use. You can also record directions in your own voice.

For that relatively small difference, you're doubling the storage to 32GB and getting wireless charging, an ad-free lock screen, and a front light that automatically adjusts to your surroundings—on top of the same sharp seven-inch display, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life as the standard Paperwhite, as noted by this PCMag review.

Its seven-inch screen shows that color content at 150ppi while keeping text at a sharp 300ppi, and you can mark passages in multiple highlight colors to keep your notes organized. That said, colors are noticeably more muted than on a conventional tablet, and battery life tops out at eight weeks, compared with 12 weeks on the Paperwhite.

The Like-New Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $243.99 from $287.99, making it just $23 more than the standard like-new Colorsoft. For that modest increase, you're getting twice the storage at 32GB, which is particularly useful for comics, manga, and graphic novels that take up more space than regular ebooks, along with wireless charging, an automatically adjusting front light, and an ad-free lock screen. However, as PCMag notes in its review, the color display produces more subdued tones than a conventional tablet, so the Paperwhite remains the more economical choice if you primarily read novels.

The Like-New Kindle Scribe (16GB) is down to $284.99 from $359.99, the biggest dollar discount in this roundup. Unlike the other Kindles here, it's built for reading and writing, with a 10.2-inch, 300ppi glare-free display and a Premium Pen with an eraser and shortcut button—making it the most versatile option for readers who want an e-reader that doubles as a digital notebook.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, but prices aren’t always what they seem. Use a price tracker to make sure you’re getting the best deal, or refer to guides like our live blog that use price trackers for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

#3423. Today’s macOS updates fix security gap involving eMudhra certificates

Apple today released macOS updates that address a security gap involving compromised eMudhra certificates, after initially blocking them in Safari, Mail, and other apps in October. Here are the details.

A few weeks ago, Mozilla reported that private keys of eight intermediate certificate authorities operated by eMudhra, an Indian digital certification company, had been compromised.

In essence, these certificates are used to establish trust in digital certificates that verify website identities and enable secure connections.

With access to the compromised private keys, bad actors could potentially create fraudulent certificates that appear legitimate, allowing them to impersonate websites and intercept sensitive user information.

In response to the compromise, Apple began automatically blocking the affected certificates on October 19, followed by additional protections on October 23.

These changes were delivered through automatic certificate configuration updates, meaning users didn’t need to install a macOS update to be protected.

While these measures protected Safari, Mail, and apps that use Apple’s networking and security frameworks, they didn’t cover all of macOS, as certain command-line tools, including curl and git, could still accept the compromised certificates.

At the time, Apple published a support article with instructions for administrators to manually address this remaining security gap, while promising a fix in a future macOS update.

Today, Apple updated the document to confirm that the fix is now available.

As Apple explains, macOS 27.2.1, macOS 26.7.3, and macOS 15.8.3, released earlier today, prevent the affected command-line tools from accepting the compromised certificates, eliminating the need for administrators to manually address the issue.

The updates also remove five root CA certificates from /etc/ssl/cert.pem, including three additional eMudhra certificates that weren’t part of Apple’s original manual workaround.

Still, for users who are unable to install the latest macOS updates, Apple continues to provide instructions for manually addressing the issue in its support document, along with the names and SHA-256 fingerprints of the 12 affected certificates and five root CA certificates removed by the updates.

Apple also notes that “some apps and tools include their own list of root CA certificates and don’t use Apple’s block or /etc/ssl/cert.pem,” and advises users to contact the developer of those apps and tools.

To read Apple’s full support document, follow this link.

Google has officially launched Gemini 4 Carbon, its most powerful AI model yet, and some of its most interesting capabilities go far beyond what most users have previously done with a chatbot.

The new model is designed to take on complicated projects that require planning, problem-solving and several steps to complete. That could mean building an interactive website, making sense of hundreds of pages of documents or analyzing information that would take hours to sort through manually.

Still, it's worth knowing what Google's latest model can do. Here are five practical ways to put Gemini 4 Carbon to work, along with prompts to get started.

Getting a handle on your finances usually means digging through statements, adding up expenses and figuring out where your money is going. Even with a spreadsheet, it's time-consuming.

Gemini 4 Carbon is designed to analyze dense documents and spreadsheets while keeping track of information across multiple sources. That makes it worth trying for tasks such as comparing monthly expenses, spotting recurring subscriptions and identifying spending patterns.

You could upload sample financial data and ask Carbon to group your expenses into categories, calculate totals and suggest where you might be able to save. Of course, you'll want to be sure to verify the totals yourself. AI can still make calculation errors, and it's best to avoid uploading sensitive account information.

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

Try this prompt: Analyze these three months of household expenses. Categorize every transaction, identify recurring subscriptions and show me where my spending has increased. Create a monthly budget with realistic savings goals and explain which expenses I should review first. Double-check your calculations before presenting the results.

This might be one of the most exciting uses for Carbon, especially if you've ever had an idea for a website but didn't know where to begin.

Google says that Carbon can work through complex coding tasks, design interfaces and check its own work for errors. The company also provides a dedicated AI Studio environment for building full-stack web apps and 3D experiences.

For example, you could ask it to build a family vacation planner that organizes your itinerary, tracks your budget and keeps everyone on the same page.

Instead of spending hours learning to code, you can describe what you want and have Carbon generate a starting point. You can then ask for changes to the layout, additional features or fixes when something doesn't work. For this one, use Google AI Studio's app-building environment, where Carbon can help create and verify a working app.Try this prompt: Build an interactive family vacation planner with a five-day itinerary, packing checklist, budget tracker and countdown to departure. Make it colorful, easy to use on a phone and simple enough for kids to understand. Include editable activities and check that all buttons and calculations work.

Most AI chatbots can explain a math problem or summarize a science lesson. Carbon is designed to go further when a question requires multiple stages of reasoning.

Google says the model has improved capabilities in scientific reasoning, including working through complex problems, exploring different approaches and checking results.

For students, that could mean turning a confusing textbook chapter into a personalized study guide or getting a detailed explanation of a problem rather than simply receiving the answer.It's important to remember that more reasoning doesn't guarantee a correct answer. But Carbon's ability to work through complicated problems could make it useful when a quick explanation isn't enough.

Parents could also use Carbon to create practice questions tailored to their child's grade level. I recently did that to help my middle schooler prepare for a science test. The interactive experience actually made studying fun since it was gamified.

Try this prompt: I'm studying Newton's laws of motion and struggling to understand the difference between force, mass and acceleration. Explain the concepts using everyday examples a seventh grader would understand. Then create five practice questions, starting easy and getting harder. Include the answers separately and explain each solution step by step.

We've all encountered documents that seem to go on forever, whether it's an insurance policy, a research report or the terms of a new service. Knowing what's important and what we can skip is almost impossible when faced with several pages of documentation.

Carbon supports a context window of up to 1 million tokens, allowing it to process large amounts of information within a single request. It can also work with images, audio and video alongside text.

Google says Carbon has improved at grounding responses in source material, particularly when analyzing complicated PDFs, spreadsheets and presentations.

For everyday users, the appeal is straightforward. Instead of spending hours hunting for important details, you can ask Carbon to find the information that matters and explain it in plain English. The ability to trace answers back to their sources is particularly useful here, although you'll still want to check important details against the original documents.

Try this prompt: Compare these two insurance policies and identify the biggest differences in coverage, deductibles, exclusions and out-of-pocket costs. Create a side-by-side comparison table, cite the relevant pages and flag anything that isn't clearly explained. Don't make assumptions about missing information.

You don't have to be a game developer to come up with an idea for a fun game. With Carbon, you can try turning that idea into something interactive.

Google has highlighted the model's ability to work on complex coding projects, including 3D scenes and interactive applications. Carbon can generate code, investigate problems and make revisions as it works toward a finished result.

That opens the door to creating simple browser games, interactive learning activities or even personalized games for kids.Google AI Studio's app-building environment is the best place to start with a project like this. A more ambitious game may still need multiple rounds of adjustments, but you can experiment without writing every line of code yourself.

Try this prompt: Create a colorful browser game where a cartoon cat collects fish while avoiding obstacles. Include three difficulty levels, a score counter, sound effects and a restart button. Make the controls simple enough for a six-year-old to use. Test the game and fix any problems you find.

Gemini 4 Carbon spends more time reasoning and verifying its work, so it's worth noting that it can be slower and use more tokens than Gemini 4 Argon. For writing an email, planning dinner or asking a straightforward question, Argon may be the more practical choice.

For complex projects, though, Carbon offers something more interesting. It gives users a way to take an idea that might otherwise require specialized software, technical knowledge or hours of manual work and see how far AI can get them.
